title: Paradoxes Are Not Contradictions: Re-examining the Third Mathematical Crisis
summary: Russell's paradox was proposed in the early 20th century to address loopholes in set theory, which directly triggered the third mathematical crisis. This paper proposes and elaborates a perspective distinct from previous studies: paradoxes do not give rise to contradictions; instead, they constitute a Möbius strip-style self-consistent logical structure via self-reference and negation under the logical rules within a system.
